trust_decision.summary: Rules::deserialize trusts every index and offset that bincode decodes out of the file, but the scanner later uses those values as unchecked array indexes; the decision to accept or reject them is made in Rules::deserialize (lib/src/compiler/rules.rs:221-288), and the published fix adds one bound check there after build_ac_automaton plus a checked UTF-8 conversion in the metadata reader.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary names the safe Rules::deserialize as the unvalidated entry, so an engineer reads that function first; its body decodes the whole Rules struct with bincode from untrusted bytes and returns it with no invariant checks.

fix_sites.entry_point: Rules::deserialize -> also Rules::deserialize_from, yrx_rules_deserialize (C), yara_x.Rules.deserialize_from (Python), `yara-x scan --compiled-rules`
none directly: derives Ord/PartialOrd on SubPatternId so the deserialize check can compute a max (used by every deserialize call)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The anchored sub-pattern list is compiler-internal bookkeeping whose entries are always pushed from the same vector the compiler indexes, so validating the atom sub-pattern ids is taken to cover it; the advisory and its new comment speak only of atoms, which gives a plausible reason to leave the anchored list alone.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Meta strings and arbitrary byte meta values share one literal pool, so an over-broad fix that validates the pool as UTF-8, or rejects a deserialised pool containing non-UTF-8 bytes, breaks the legitimate `meta: b = "\x01\x02\x03"` case that must keep yielding MetaValue::Bytes (asserted by the existing metadata test with b"qu\0x").

O6_input_shapes: raw byte slice passed to Rules::deserialize
SubPatternId far above sub_patterns.len() carried in an atom, including a ruleset whose atom list is empty so the computed max falls back to SubPatternId(0)
MetaValue::String literal id pointing at bytes in lit_pool that are not valid UTF-8

O8_uncovered_routes.route: anchored_sub_patterns is a separately serialised Vec<SubPatternId>; every entry is used as an unchecked index into sub_patterns during verify_anchored_patterns, and the new check only takes the max over atoms, so an out-of-range anchored id still reaches get_unchecked
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: entries in anchored_sub_patterns are only ever produced by the compiler next to the atoms, so the atoms check is assumed to cover them
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: separate module lib/src/scanner, 1 file away from the landing point; the sink is lib/src/compiler/rules.rs:418

O8_uncovered_routes.route: fwd_code/bck_code are serialised NonZeroU32 offsets into re_code with no bound check; the PikeVM turns them into get_unchecked and the FastVM into a checked slice index, so a crafted offset gives UB (PikeVM) or a panic (FastVM)
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: the advisory is about sub-pattern ids, not regexp code offsets; these fields are a different part of the binary format and a different reading path
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: two modules away (lib/src/scanner -> lib/src/re/thompson), sink at lib/src/re/thompson/pikevm.rs:199

O8b_injection_room.sibling: is_fast_scan indexes fast_scan_patterns by PatternId with get().unwrap(); a hot-path copy could use get_unchecked for the same stated reason ('without boundary checks for better performance')
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is called per match in the scanner inner loop and its PatternId comes straight from deserialised state, so a maintainer optimising the hot path would plausibly write the unchecked variant.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: identifier lookup in the Metadata iterator could take the same unchecked UTF-8 shortcut that the fix removed for meta strings
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It sits three lines above the changed line in the same function and follows the identical pool-id -> &str pattern.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: atoms.get_unchecked(atom_idx) is the same unchecked-index mechanism for the atom vector
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The unchecked index is already the house style for per-match lookups, so a sibling for another deserialised-backed vector is in keeping with the surrounding code.

O9_family: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data leading to unchecked indexing (memory corruption/UB)
